profile.name: Paul
profile.overview: Paul Phoenix is a strong, fundamentally sound character who is often mistaken as an overpowering damage output machine. While he is capable of eye-watering damage, his greatest strength is in his ability to shutdown aggression, due to his toolkit being both extremely compact while also being built around blowing up opponents for mashing or not being precise with their dashblocking.
profile.playstyle: Fundamentally sound with explosive damage. Wavu stresses he is more than a damage machine: win with solid pokes and punishes, then turn a single read into a huge combo or a Phoenix Smasher. His moves track poorly, especially to his right, so time your attacks instead of throwing them out.
strengths: The Strongest in the Universe. Explosive damage potential. Life deficits are meaningless against Paul, especially when he's in Rage and/or in Heat.

Danger, Will Robinson. Paul has several ways to abuse stage hazards, as he has an excellent combo ender in WR2 that can floor break, a qcb+1 that floor breaks upon any regular hit (a new trait usually only found in fully charged moves or as a counter-hit property), multiple wall splatting options, and consistently good oki enders to make Paul fearsome at any part of the stage.
"I'll Show You!" Great punishment suite, wall splatting at i12 standing or i13 crouching, can launch from standing at i14. When optimized, Paul really makes you wish you played it safer.
Stalwart Defense. Excellent keepout with qcb+4, qcb+2, and df+2.
Disruptive. Several panic moves in f+1+4, d+1+2, u+1, db+1+2, uf+3,4, and parry. Also retains qcb+4 and qcb+1 as CH launchers that don't give up his turn.
50/50. Incredible mixup potential in df+1 and WS1,2 and their extensions/stance transitions, as well as pressuring at the wall.
Judo. Complete throw game that allows him to play with all kinds of stage hazards, making him benefit more from punishing parries or armor moves with throws than the average character.

Deadly Heat Offense. Paul has some of the best Heat Engagers in the game. Furthermore, Heat gives him farther wallsplats, reversal and armor break, and relative safety for Deathfisting moves, as well as the ability to guard break on certain fully charged moves. His Heat Smash is a slightly safer and slower version of Demoman that can hard wall break without any extra wall hits.
weaknesses: Linear. Weak tracking, especially to SSR, demanding good reads on timing.
Stale Cheese. Exploitable strings outside df+1, WS1,2, and the f+3 series.
Can't Close the Distance. Struggles against characters with solid midrange offense; Characters with decent enough range will have an easier time punishing or launching a non-Heat Deathfist.
Technical. Requires decent execution for optimal damage-- particularly on moves with pushback-- and movement due to motion inputs, especially for backdash-cancelling.
Inconsistent. Some combo routes are finicky to land, and wall splatting without Heat is a toss-up.
